title: Psalm 77:19
paragraphs:
“Your path led through the sea,
your way through the mighty waters,
though your footprints were not seen.”

God was moving.
But nobody could trace His steps.

Israel saw the sea.
They saw danger.
They saw no road, no bridge, no map.
But God made a way where there was no visible way.
That is the ache of faith, isn’t it?

You pray.
You wait.
You cry.
And heaven feels silent.

No footprints.
No explanation.
No clear outline.
Yet Psalm 77:19 reminds us: God does some of His greatest work in places that look impossible and feel unreadable. The sea was not an obstacle to Him. It was His roadway.
Just because you cannot track Him does not mean He has abandoned you.

The cross looked like chaos too.
Darkness.
Blood.
Silence.
A sealed tomb.

But through that unbearable sea, God was carving out salvation. Jesus walked into the deepest waters of sin, judgment, and death—and came out victorious, so sinners like us could be redeemed by grace.
So when you cannot see His footprints, cling to His character.

He is still holy.
Still wise.
Still present.
Still making a way.

Prayer:
Lord, when I cannot see where You are leading, teach me to trust Your heart. In my confusion, be my peace. In my waiting, be my anchor. Thank You that Jesus is the proof You never abandon Your people. Amen.

Truth to carry today:
Invisible footprints do not mean an absent God.
